item.title: Dairy Beef Club Meetings
item.description:
Dairy Beef Club Meetings slmacneil Tue, 10/27/2026 - 15:32

The Dairy Beef Club is a new opportunity for producers across the dairy-beef chain to connect and learn peer to peer. 

The DBC is open to dairy producers, nursery growers, backgrounders, and finishers involved in dairy-beef or interested in becoming involved in the production chain. 

The pilot will include in-person learning sessions, farm tours, and virtual presentation. Topics will  focus on real production challenges and practical solutions that can benefit your farm. 

What's in it for you? 

  • Learn from other producers.
  • Get practical information
  • Make connections.
  • Improve your bottom line.
  • Help direct group learning.

Topics to be covered:

  • Building a resilient Beef Calf
  • Beef Calf Health Management
  • Maritime Livestock Price Insurance
  • Backgrounding Beef Calves on pasture
  • Dairy Crosses in Feedlot (400-S00lbs)
  • Calf Performance Targets and Indicators
  • Handling Systems and Data Collection
  • Finishing (800-1500Ibs)
  • Farm Tour
  • Producer Panels

Check out the Calendar for more information:

  • November 
    • Nov 3 - OLeary Club
    • Nov 10 - Monatgue Club
    • Nov 12 - Charlottetown Club
    • Nov 26 - Virtual Meeting
  • December
    • Dec 1 - O'Leary Club
    • Dec 2 - Monatgue Club
    • Dec 3 - Charlottetown Club
    • Dec 16 - Virtual Meeting

For more information, contact:

item.title: Feedback wanted on proposed changes to the Prince Edward Island Lands Protection Act
item.description:
Feedback wanted on proposed changes to the Prince Edward Island Lands Protection Act jenniferdhogan Tue, 10/27/2026 - 13:42

The province is inviting residents and interested stakeholders to provide feedback on proposed changes to the Prince Edward Island Lands Protection Act.

As part of the Department of Land and Environment's ongoing review of provincial legislation, a consultation document is available online for public review.

"We want to hear from Islanders to help ensure our legislation remains effective and reflects the needs of our communities. Public input is an important part of the legislative process, and we encourage interested residents and organizations to share their perspectives."

- Minister of Land and Environment Darlene Compton

The following legislation is available for review:

  • An Act to Amend the Prince Edward Island Lands Protection Act (No. 2)

Comments can be submitted by email to DeptLE@gov.pe.ca until November 10, 2026.

For more information and to review the consultation document, visit Department of Land and Environmental Public Consultations.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
